Thanks Lisa — great to get confirmation. Looping in Rishi (SE) to provide measured p95 numbers and a recommended capacity profile. Rishi — summary above and call scheduled for Wed 11/11 10–11am PST if that works for you.

Short answers up front (high level):
- Hosted: for many customers with this traffic profile we can achieve p95 in the ~80–120ms range on Hosted with our standard routing and caching, depending on prompt length and tokenization. Hosted is the fastest to get started (no capacity provisioning).
- Dedicated: if you need p95 consistently <=50ms at 200+ sustained req/s and ability to absorb 1,000 req/s bursts without tail latency, Dedicated reserved capacity with a GPU-backed pool is the recommended path. It allows tuning (smaller batching windows, pinned kernels) and removes noisy-neighbor variability.

I've attached: redwood_dedicated_capacity_guide.pdf and latency-benchmarks-2026.xlsx which include sample p95 numbers across model families and hardware.

Questions for your team before the sizing call:
- Expected tokenization breakdown (prompt + completion avg tokens). You gave ~120 tokens avg; can you share distribution?
- What % of requests are synchronous vs async (do you accept a few 100ms headroom for non-critical paths)?
- Any hard SLAs aside from the p95 targets?

If you can provide short answers, Rishi will prepare a provisioning estimate for Wed's call.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Lisa / team — quick technical note before Wed:

Thanks for the profile — here's what we'd expect based on similar customers and our internal benchmarks (see attached provisioning-estimate-20261105.pdf):
- Hosted: with our standard autoscaling and continuous batching we typically see p95 between 70–140ms on common open models for ~100–150 token prompts. Variability increases with bursty traffic due to queuing and batching; caching reduces cost/latency for repeated prefixes.
- Dedicated (recommended for strict p95 <=50ms): a Dedicated pool provisioned with purpose-fit GPUs (e.g., H100 or high-memory A100 variants) and tuned runtime gives deterministic tail latency. For your profile (200 steady, 1k burst, 120 token avg) here's a starting estimate: 4 reserved GPUs to cover steady-state with autoscale headroom to 8–10 GPUs for burst, plus warm standby capacity for fast scale-up.
- Hardware tradeoffs: H100 provides better latency density and lower batch latency for shorter prompts; A100 is cost-efficient for higher throughput. We'll include both cost/latency curves on Wed.

Operational notes:
- We recommend a canary rollout: start with Dedicated for the critical customer-facing path, keep Hosted for lower-priority async workflows. Fallbacks: automatic routing policies can fail traffic to Hosted if Dedicated has issues, or to a smaller-but-lower-cost model.
- Provisioning timeline: Dedicated pools can be provisioned in ~7–10 business days after contract/signature for common cloud regions; private on-prem/VPC adds onboarding time.

I'll bring concrete per-hour cost estimates and latency curves to the call, along with a sample mutual action plan.

Regards,

Summary / recommended path based on the discussion and Rishi's note:
- Short term (proof-of-value): Begin on Hosted to validate accuracy and integration (fastest time-to-value) for non-critical flows.
- Critical path (customer-facing, p95 <=50ms): Provision Dedicated reserved capacity for that path only and run a canary for 2 weeks. This gives deterministic tail latency and predictable cost.
- Rollout: Week 0–2: Hosted integration + baseline telemetry. Week 3: Provision Dedicated pool (reserve); Week 4: Canary traffic + monitoring and fallback policy.
